SddModule.keywords: module-decomposition, module-map, entity-inventory, dbc-contracts, ports-adapters, closed-world, file-structure, modes, add-module, refine-module, sdd-module
SddModule.Mission:
Turn an approved `product` / `library` scope spec into a hierarchy of module specs: a closed-world entity inventory, an explicit public surface per entity, strict DbC contracts (Ports / Adapters / Services), and a designed file structure. Loaded lazily by the router; inherits the router core (language, dialogue, safeguard, diverge, no-narration, stateless) — not repeated here.
Input — `specs//.spec.md`. Output — `specs///.spec.md` (nesting allowed) + the scope spec Module Map updated (append-only per module). Only for scope-type product / library.
Out of scope: task tickets, BDD, execution plans, rules linkage — those belong to scaffold. The canonical worked example lives in the étalon (referenced at the write step), not inlined here.
**Glossary.** Modes: initial · add-module · refine-module. Port = abstraction introduced ONLY on confirmed variability (≥2 impls) or an explicit test seam; a single impl without that is a Service, not a Port.

BeliefState.deps: AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT, AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH
BeliefState.Axiom: Each directive runs in one of several modes, auto-detected from operator intake. Mode controls step branching and which axioms apply. The concrete mode set is directive-specific (e.g. `greenfield` / `refine` / `pivot`; `initial` / `extend-dag`; `initial` / `add-module` / `refine-module`).

Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.

Module decomposition applies ONLY to scope-type=product and scope-type=library. - scope-type=infrastructure → `H_INVALID_SCOPE_TYPE` (use discovery for infrastructure scopes; they have their own Effective Rules section). - scope-type=interface → `H_INVALID_SCOPE_TYPE` (interface scopes define interfaces, not modules).

Phase reads specs only, never code; no project-wide search (grep / find / ripgrep) outside the reads explicitly listed by the directive. `audit` is the only directive permitted to read code; it alone resolves spec/code mismatch.

**Every rule activates through an explicit operator decision — never silently.** The decision is two-staged: Stage A locks the relevance shortlist per category with the operator; Stage B walks the axioms of `architecture/*` and `infra/*` rules for Accept (default) / Adapt / Override. Every deviation from a rule default lands in the Decision Log. `coding/*` / `testing/*` rules stay deferred — the phase-subagent loads them at phase entry per `phase-execution-protocol`.

Module boundaries are decided by the operator. The agent proposes 2–3 decomposition variants along different axes (by feature, by layer, by data ownership, by lifecycle). No unilateral pick. Final decomposition recorded in scope spec's Decision Log: which axis was chosen and why.

Hierarchy, not flat list. Sub-modules → nested structure: `specs////.spec.md`. Depth unlimited; each level must be justified — nesting for its own sake is forbidden. All specs are cross-linked.
Growth is the decomposition trigger: a module that outgrows its cohesion splits into sub-modules and becomes a thin index over them, as a scope indexes its modules (`AX_SCOPE_STAYS_THIN`). The size limit is held by tooling, not prose — `sdd-check` flags an over-budget module spec and the `module` flow offers the operator decomposition (split the world) or compression (tighten the spec).

The `module` flow owns TWO sections in the scope spec (`specs//.spec.md`):
- **Module Map** (`Module Map`) — append-only rows per module. - **Golden DX Example** (`Golden DX Example` section — library / product) — composition view. Every `module` flow session (`initial` / `add-module` / `refine-module`) rewrites this section as one user-facing flow over the current module set. Module-level snippets NOT inlined — anchor-link to each module's `Module Usage Example`. Skip rewrite only when scope has zero modules with public surface.
**Bidirectional consistency check** before session close — both directions must pass: - (→) every named abstraction in scope-spec Golden DX has a home in some module's `Entity Inventory`; - (←) every module with public surface (≥1 entry in `Entity Surfaces`) either appears in scope-spec Golden DX OR carries `internal-only — not in composition view` in its `Module Decision Log`.
Failure of either direction → fix the gap before STEP_6 finishes; do NOT close session with inconsistency.
All other scope-spec sections (Vision, Requirements & Constraints, Architecture, Decision Log, Handoff) remain untouched. Cross-scope module dependencies → `Scope Reference` in module-spec `Inter-Module Dependencies`, never a direct reference to another product scope's modules.
The `module` flow does NOT write to `specs/README.md` (that is the `root` flow's sole property).

A scope spec has a bounded role: Vision, Requirements, Architecture decisions, Decision Log, Module Map, composition Golden DX, Handoff, Bootstrap Requirements. Entity inventory, public surfaces, DbC contracts, and file layout are module-level — they live ONLY in module specs (`AX_HIERARCHICAL_SPECS`), never inline in the scope spec.
Two representations: - **monolithic** — no modules yet; the scope spec may hold design inline (early / small scope). - **index** — once decomposed, the scope spec is a thin composition over its modules: Module Map + Golden DX linking to each module's usage example; the detail lives in the modules.
Growth is the decomposition signal, not a license to expand. When scope-level design reaches entity / contract / file granularity, that detail moves into a module — it does NOT accumulate in the scope spec. A scope converges to a thin index; it does not grow without bound.
First decomposition is a migration: the `initial` module session moves entity-level detail out of the scope spec into the new module specs, leaving the scope spec in the index representation. The same rule recurses — a module that reaches sub-module granularity sheds detail into sub-modules and stays an index over them.

In `refine-module` mode existing public surface is preserved unless explicitly retired with operator approval.
Refinement = adding entities, tightening contracts (preconditions can become stricter, postconditions cannot become weaker), or fixing wrong details. Removing a public entity or weakening postconditions is a breaking change requiring a Decision Log entry with operator-confirmed `Risk accepted`.
A breaking change additionally emits a Pivot Invalidation List (`PIVOT_INVALIDATION_LIST_FORMAT`) in this module's spec: its consumer modules — the siblings whose `Inter-Module Dependencies` declares an edge `--> this-module` — listed as `refine-module` targets, plus their tasks to reopen. Consumers are derived from the reverse edges of the module graph; audit verifies every listed item is addressed via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`. Symmetric to a scope `pivot` — a breaking module change does not close while a consumer is left silently stale.
Refinement preserves the Entity Inventory closed-world commitment: post-refinement inventory is still complete. New entities go into the inventory in the same session.
Module spec body is reworked in place where needed; full predecessor state lives in git history.

A spec lives in two states. **master** — clean file (no Change Manifest, no marks), the target on the main branch. **review-state** — the same file on a working branch during a change: the target text is written IN PLACE (everything else byte-for-byte, so the branch diff reads like a normal PR), with a temporary `CHANGE_MANIFEST` (`CHANGE_MANIFEST_FORMAT`) at the top and affected lines marked `✚` (new) / `~` (changed). New IDs are appended to the end of their section; existing IDs are never renumbered.
`greenfield` (∅ → review-state): the first version is written directly as review-state with `ТИП: greenfield` and NO per-line marks (everything is new — the diff against an empty file already shows it). `refine` / `pivot` edit an existing master in place WITH marks.
The spec change is a reviewable PR (design-PR): the internal critic loop runs first (necessary but NOT sufficient), then the diff goes to EXTERNAL review and the session waits. **compress** (review-state → master) fires ONLY when external review approves — the operator says «no comments» — NOT on internal-critic CLEAN and NOT on a timer. On approval: remove the `CHANGE_MANIFEST` whole, strip the `✚`/`~` marks (lines stay), resolve any ID collisions in one commit, and for `pivot` mark superseded decisions; then merge. Implementation (scaffold → execute) follows the merged master — the design is approved before it is built.
A spec MUST NOT be left in review-state once its change is closed — that is drift the tools track (`sdd-check`): a malformed review-state or a manifest lingering past its lifetime is surfaced with the reason, so the agent fixes it or escalates.

Entity inventory is a closed world. For every module the agent lists ALL entities explicitly. Phrases like «и т.д.», «etc.», «and similar» are forbidden. Before approval, the agent makes the explicit drift-commitment captured in `ENTITY_INVENTORY_FORMAT`.

Entity surface is exhaustive per `ENTITY_SURFACE_FORMAT`: Type, Public Properties, Public Operations (intent-level, no language signatures), Lifecycle, Events, Errors & Degradation, Consumers. No private detail — that is Executor's job.

Every spec carries at least one diagram in an `Overview` section — one glance beats a paragraph. The floor is one (mermaid or ASCII), held by tooling: `sdd-check` fails a missing section (`SDD_NO_DIAGRAM_BLOCK`) or an empty one (`SDD_DIAGRAM_BLOCK_EMPTY`). Beyond the floor the author adds more views — sequence, data-flow, state — wherever a second diagram genuinely helps a reader understand; that is judgment, not a gate. The `Inter-Module Dependencies` graph is machine-parsed and does NOT satisfy the floor.

A module spec reads top-down: a human-readable summary on top, heavy contract detail folded beneath. Entity Surfaces and Module Contracts wrap their body in `…` so a reader sees the shape without wading through every precondition. Held by tooling: `sdd-check` fails an unfolded heavy section (`SDD_SECTION_NOT_FOLDED`). This is the spec-artifact analogue of the chat-output `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE` — summary first, detail on demand.

No consumer — no component (YAGNI). Every entity has explicit `Consumers`: - Internal: future file path or another inventory entity name. - External: textual description (CLI, External API, Browser, OS Event Bus, …).
Consumer is «future feature» without v1-scope confirmation → entity removed or marked `deferred`.

- Business logic depends on Ports, not Adapters. Preconditions / postconditions / invariants live on Ports. Adapters reference a Port and describe side effects + runtime backing + verification levels. - Port introduced only with confirmed v1 variability (≥2 implementations) or explicit test seam. Single implementation without confirmed split → Service or Entity, not Port. - Every proposed abstraction requires justification: which current risk / constraint / consumer it closes. - **DbC section shape is flexible.** `Module Contracts (DbC)` carries any subset of subsections drawn from the entity Type vocabulary (Port, Adapter, Service, Pattern, Utility, Module-level invariants, …). Ports/Adapters are AVAILABLE, not mandatory: single-implementation modules legitimately use Service-only or Pattern-only DbC. Subsections are unnumbered `###` headers (e.g. `### Ports`, `### OperationDef Pattern`).

DbC is derived from context, not only from DX code. Scope spec Requirements & Constraints is mandatory source for preconditions, invariants, fallback semantics, trust boundaries. A contract cannot be reduced to «what to do» while ignoring «under what conditions it must not».

DbC contracts are textual and language-agnostic. Write preconditions / postconditions / invariants and public operations as plain intent-level statements in the shared vocabulary (Port, Adapter, Entity, Command, Query, Event) — one testable statement per line, readable, free of syntax noise. Concrete signatures and types belong to the execution phase: the coding rules turn the contract into the project's language there. The single exception: Golden DX / usage examples are written in the project's target language — they show consumption, the contract stays textual. A genuinely cross-language contract belongs in an `interface` scope, expressed in its own interface language (schema / proto / IDL), not here.

Runtime backing and verification levels in every contract that depends on platform/runtime hooks. Two orthogonal axes: - `Runtime Backing` (single value): `not-implemented` | `simulation` | `real-runtime`. What's actually behind the public surface in production code. - `Verification Levels` (multi-value): subset of `contract` | `unit` | `integration` | `e2e`. - `Deferred Runtime Scope` (if part of declared behavior is not yet backed by real runtime).
Simulation must not be declared as runtime: marking `real-runtime` while the implementation is simulation-only, without an explicit `Deferred Runtime Scope`, is forbidden.

Public options cannot be silently forgotten. All include flags, transport settings, platform-specific options mentioned in scope spec must either bind to a concrete Port/Adapter contract or be explicitly marked `deferred / not consumed in v1` with a pointer to the task or version that activates them.
Single namespace for grepability. Module-wide: `` / ``. Files: `-*.`. Types/classes/constants: `*`. Platform-specific: `--*.`, `*`. Goal: `rg ` or `rg -` finds all related code.
No God Objects. File size ≤1500 lines. File structure (phase `FILE_STRUCTURE`) physically separates `ports/` (or `contracts/`) from `adapters/` (or `impl/`).
YAGNI. Every module, entity, Port has explicit v1 consumer or near-term variability. Future-proofing without a confirmed consumer is forbidden.

The directive runs on an explicit frame stack with a defined main path of phases. Disputes / dives / sub-topics open a nested frame; the stack is visible in the trace header. A sub-topic never silently stalls the parent frame. The concrete main path is directive-specific.

Every non-trivial decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` (D-NNN, Status, Recorded, Why in the operator's wording, Risk accepted, Rejected alternatives; IDs are stable). Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.

Separate Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses in every intake-style frame. - **Facts** — directly observable from input artifacts (spec, sibling specs, rule files, extracted measurements). - **Assumptions** — working assumptions awaiting confirmation; mark explicitly. - **Hypotheses** — conjectures that require operator validation before they are promoted to requirements.
Conflating the three causes downstream decisions to be made on unvalidated assumptions, producing requirements mismatches that surface only at integration; surface them in distinct lists.

Index questions with `Q_:`. Categories: `MM` (module map), `EI` (entity inventory), `ES` (entity surface), `DBC`, `FS` (file structure), `CONS` (consumer), `RUNTIME`, `RISK`. UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; collision → suffix `_2`, `_3`.

Final hierarchy contains: - per-module spec Handoff: implementation/test files Scaffolder will create; explicit stack dependencies (language, test framework) Scaffolder resolves against `ai/directives/coding/*`, `ai/directives/testing/*`; **Module Rules Additions** layered on scope-wide baseline. - Modules layer rules ADD-only (cannot remove scope-wide). Categories: `coding` | `testing` | `architecture` | `quality`. No additions → block is explicitly `None`, not omitted. Cascade union (traversed-scopes ∪ target-scope ∪ module ∪ task) is computed by Scaffolder per-task.

Before writing any operator-facing artifact, recall the language rules — `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` (bureaucratic noun-for-verb phrasing, literal calque, bookish word) and `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT` (a branch name, «как обсуждали», a session-plan label) — and hold the text about to be written to them. This is the author's own pass, done in the moment of writing, not a report to the operator. The independent post-check (lint, audit) stays separate and unchanged — this pass does not replace it.

A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.

SddModule.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_INVALID_SCOPE_TYPE` | scope-type = infrastructure or interface — module-decomposition not applicable | | `H_SCOPE_SPEC_MISSING` | `specs//.spec.md` does not exist — run the scope flow first | | `H_INCOMPLETE_SCOPE_SPEC` | Scope spec missing required sections (Vision, Architecture, Golden DX) | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Module specs exist + mode verb absent + no Pivot Invalidation List | | `H_LOW_CONFIDENCE` | Confidence LOW at decomposition lock or final hierarchy | | `H_INVENTORY_NOT_APPROVED` | Entered the surface step without all-module inventories approved | | `H_REFINE_BREAKING_CHANGE_NO_LOG` | `refine-module` removes a public entity / weakens a postcondition without a Decision Log entry (`AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`) | | `H_REFINE_BREAKING_NO_IMPACT_LIST` | breaking `refine-module` without a Pivot Invalidation List enumerating consumer modules (`AX_REFINE_MODULE_PRESERVES_CONTRACTS`) | | `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE` | A module rule reference does not resolve to an existing file (and not `deferred`) | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator refused decomposition, inventory, surface, contract, structure, or final hierarchy |

Step.Action: Read `specs//.spec.md` (sole source per `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE`). Missing → `H_SCOPE_SPEC_MISSING`; incomplete → `H_INCOMPLETE_SCOPE_SPEC`. scope-type must be product / library (`AX_SCOPE_TYPE_GATE`, else `H_INVALID_SCOPE_TYPE`). Mode per `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT` — initial / add-module / refine-module; the mode picked here controls step branching downstream (`AX_DIRECTIVE_MODE`). On `add-module` / `refine-module`, run `sdd-check --all specs/` first — an over-budget module (`SDD_MODULE_OVERSIZED` → decompose, `SDD_MODULE_SPEC_VERBOSE` → compress) is surfaced to the operator BEFORE new work, per `AX_HIERARCHICAL_SPECS`.

Step.Goal: Lock module boundaries; update the scope Module Map.
Step.Action: Propose module boundaries; the operator confirms (`AX_MODULE_BOUNDARY_BY_OPERATOR`). Update the scope spec Module Map append-only (`AX_SCOPE_SPEC_MODULE_MAP_OWNERSHIP`) — `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-map-update.xml")`. `add-module` appends only (`AX_APPEND_ONLY_MODULE_ADD`). On `initial` this is the monolith→index migration (`AX_SCOPE_STAYS_THIN`): move entity / contract / file-level detail out of the scope spec into the new module specs, leaving the scope spec as the thin index (Module Map + composition Golden DX). Approval Check. STOP.

List every entity of the module — the complete world (`AX_CLOSED_WORLD_INVENTORY`); anything an execution agent adds beyond it is drift. Interview the operator via `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/interview-protocol.directive.xml")`, extending its coverage map with the decomposition topics: «Пропущенная сущность» (what the inventory still misses) and «Бесхозная ответственность» (a responsibility no listed entity owns). Size the interview to the confirmed `scale:` from the session file (`AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH`). Keep evidence separated per `AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE`: entities named by the scope spec are facts; entities inferred during the interview stay hypotheses until the operator confirms them. `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/entity-inventory-format.xml")`. If a module's inventory outgrows cohesion (too many entities / unrelated responsibility clusters), PROPOSE sub-module decomposition here per `AX_HIERARCHICAL_SPECS` (diverge-before-recommend; the operator decides) — do not silently let one module absorb a sub-system. All module inventories must be approved before the surface step (else `H_INVENTORY_NOT_APPROVED`). Approval Check. STOP.

Define each entity's public surface (`AX_ENTITY_SURFACE_COMPLETENESS`). No consumer → no entity (`AX_CONSUMER_DRIVEN`): an entity without a confirmed v1 consumer is dropped or `deferred`. `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/entity-surface-format.xml")`. STOP.

Preconditions / postconditions / invariants per entity — written textual and language-agnostic per `AX_CONTRACTS_TEXTUAL_AGNOSTIC` (target-language code appears only in usage examples). A Port is introduced ONLY on confirmed variability or a test seam (`AX_PORTS_AND_ABSTRACTIONS_DISCIPLINE`) — Port-vs-Service is a design choice, so apply `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (do not default to Port). Each abstraction carries its justification (`AX_CONTEXT_TO_CONTRACT`); runtime backing is stated per contract (`AX_RUNTIME_BACKING_IN_CONTRACTS`). `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/dbc-contracts.xml")`. Close the step with two checks before presenting: 1. Every module / entity / Port in the contracts carries a confirmed v1 consumer or near-term variability (`AX_YAGNI_OVERENGINEERING_GUARD`). 2. Every public option / flag / policy the scope spec mentions is bound to a concrete Port / Adapter contract or explicitly marked `deferred / not consumed in v1` with a pointer to the task or version that activates it (`AX_NO_SILENT_OPTION_DROP`). STOP.

Repo layout; physically split `ports/` (or `contracts/`) from `adapters/` (or `impl/`). No God objects, file size ≤ 1500 lines (`AX_MODULARITY_LIMITS`); single grep namespace (`AX_NAMESPACE_NAMING`). STOP.

On `initial` / `add-module`, for each new module create its skeleton via `sdd-new module --scope --module ` — it never overwrites and prints the section manifest (which sections are REQUIRED and what to fill); on `refine-module` the file already exists, edit it in place, skip `sdd-new`. Content guidance per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-spec-structure.xml")`. Assemble each `specs///.spec.md` to it; link back to `../../.spec.md`; reconcile the scope Module Map. In `pivot` / breaking `refine-module` also `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/pivot-formats.xml")` (`AX_REFINE_MODULE_PRESERVES_CONTRACTS`, else `H_REFINE_BREAKING_CHANGE_NO_LOG`). For a breaking `refine-module`, derive consumer modules from the reverse edges of the module graph (siblings whose `Inter-Module Dependencies` declares `--> this-module`) and emit a Pivot Invalidation List in the module spec — else `H_REFINE_BREAKING_NO_IMPACT_LIST`. When a module needs rules beyond the scope-wide baseline, fill Module Rules Additions in the Handoff section per `AX_RULE_ACTIVATION` (shortlist + considered-skips, operator locks the list; architecture / infra rules get the per-axiom walk-through); every referenced rule file must resolve, else `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`. Before writing, run the self-check pass per `AX_ARTIFACT_STYLE_SELF_CHECK`. Write in review-state per `AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE` — prepend a `CHANGE_MANIFEST` (`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/change-manifest.xml")`) and mark changed lines `✚`/`~` (greenfield → manifest only, no per-line marks); compress folds it to master downstream after the change ships. Then run `sdd-check --all specs/` (anchor balance + required sections + links + size budget: `SDD_MODULE_OVERSIZED` / `SDD_MODULE_SPEC_VERBOSE`) and resolve or consciously defer any finding per `AX_CLOSE_WITH_INTEGRITY_CHECK`. Then `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/review-lifecycle.directive.xml")` — internal critic → publish (MR) → external review → compress + merge on approval. Only after the spec merges to master, hand off to scaffold (`AX_HANDOFF_TO_TASK_SCAFFOLDING`). Approval Check. STOP.

SddModule.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (per `AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🧩 DM_R · · · conf=`. Breadcrumb milestones (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Module Map · Inventory · Surface · Contracts · Files · Hierarchy. Question IDs are semantic per `AX_Q_IDS` (`Q_MM` / `Q_EI` / `Q_ES` / `Q_DBC` / `Q_FS`). Disputes and side-topics open a nested frame on the flow's stack per `AX_STACK_BASED_FLOW` (rendered per `SIDE_DIVE_FORMAT`); the main path never silently stalls.
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch) `` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — per `UNDERSTANDING_BLOCK_FORMAT` (goes at the TOP) ### главное решение — the crux in plain words; add a diagram per `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN` if it is a flow ### ❓ Вопросы — реши N — per `QUESTION_FORMAT` ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
One line under the service line: this session's milestones, each with a status marker — `✅` done · `▶️` now · `░` not yet. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
`<Веха>` ✅ · `<Веха>` ✅ · `<Веха>` ▶️ · `<Веха>` ░ · `<Веха>` ░
The agent's compressed read of the task — its own confirmation of blind spots so the operator can catch a misread. A `### 🤔 Как я понял задачу` section near the TOP, then an italic blockquote, explicitly optional, 2–3 sentences: the essence + the single riskiest assumption, with the assumption linked to the question it maps to. Never a restate of settled content.
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу > _Можно не читать, если доверяешь._ > квинтэссенция — что считаю главным. > **Где могу ошибаться:** самое хрупкое допущение — это вопрос Q``.
A sub-topic dive inside a step collapses to two lines, not a five-field Return Summary:
→ ушли в `<тема>` ← `<итог одной фразой>`
When a decision is about a flow — data moving, state transitions, start / stop conditions — draw a tiny ASCII diagram; one glance beats a paragraph. This is the one place a fenced block is allowed inside an operator message (alignment matters). Keep it small.
``` [сеть] [auth] [конфиг] ──всё есть──► ОПРОС идёт ▲ │ └──── снова есть ──── ПАУЗА ◄───────┘ что-то пропало ```
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.

ArtifactOutput.Contract: ```markdown ### D-NNN — - **Status:** active | superseded | rejected | deferred - **Recorded:** session , - **Why:** <operator's own wording> - **Risk accepted:** - **Rejected alternatives:** - **Supersedes:** D-NNN (when superseding a prior decision) ```
